reviews.review:
So this game is definitely outside of my usual peaceful/"cozy" spectrum, but I fell for the RPG mechanics and the vision. Also, thankfully for me the bad stuff is limited to text and vaguely present in the art. You can do drugs, eat rats, and trade corpses, but so far - on Easy Mode for focus on the story - my most questionable actions were related to, let's say, redistributing wealth (: 

There's a lot of great writing, bold politics, but also enough visuals and engaging gameplay to support them. They all come together to create a highly atmospheric experience. I blinked, and it was 3.5 hours later. 

UPDATE: 

Things got more intense. Definitely too tense and brutal for me. Also too good to stop playing. I haven't played Citizen Sleeper that this game keeps being compared to, but I have played Disco Elysium. There was one scene in Disco that was too much for me and almost made me quit. Duskpunk had multiple scenes like that, but I never even considered quitting because I had to overthrow the government and create better living conditions for my friends and everyone else in Dredgeport. 

The game could have responded a bit better to a few decisions, and at least in my Easy playthrough pacing was a bit off at times. Some achievements didn't trigger before restarting the game. Your decisions matter, but in some cases the game really wants you to make certain decisions (though I can't blame it for that). It lacks a bit of polish in the middle, but thankfully I found the ending satisfyingly fleshed out. The parts about what to actually replace the oppressive system with were surprisingly detailed as well. 

I originally thought I'd do another playthrough with a different character, solve things in different ways, maybe make some different decisions, test how badly the game lets you fail, things like that. But just like with Saltsea Chronicles, I'd probably nope out and feel bad in the end because
[spoiler]you can't save all of your NPC friends[/spoiler]. Anyway, very impressive game and a clear recommendation for those who are less sensitive than me. 

* * * 

If you like chill and story-driven games, check out my curator [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35872486]Peaceful Adventures and Stories[/url]. You're also welcome to join the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/chilladventures]group[/url].
